source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which effect is caused by sympathetic stimulation?
questions.rationale: Sympathetic: pupil dilation, tachycardia, bronchodilation, decreased peristalsis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Autonomic Nervous System (PDF p. 416)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Parasympathetic stimulation of the urinary bladder causes:
questions.rationale: Parasympathetic contracts the detrusor and relaxes sphincters, promoting voiding.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Autonomic Nervous System (PDF p. 416)
questions.quote: Urinary bladder muscle walls contracted Relax

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the highest possible Glasgow Coma Scale score?
questions.rationale: GCS ranges 3 (deep coma) to 15 (fully alert).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Glasgow Coma Scale (PDF p. 417)
questions.quote: 15=highest score; patient is fully alert and oriented

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client opens eyes to pressure, uses inappropriate words, and withdraws from pain. GCS score?
questions.rationale: Eye 2 + verbal 3 + motor 4 = 9.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Glasgow Coma Scale (PDF p. 417)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which GCS motor response is abnormal flexion?
questions.rationale: Abnormal flexion is decorticate (3); abnormal extension is decerebrate (2).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Glasgow Coma Scale (PDF p. 417)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which posture indicates more serious brain damage?
questions.rationale: Decerebrate (extension, internal rotation) is more ominous.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Abnormal Reflexes (PDF p. 419)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The Rinne and Weber tests assess cranial nerve:
questions.rationale: CN VIII: hearing (Rinne, Weber) and balance (Romberg).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cranial Nerve Assessment (PDF p. 418)
questions.quote: Test for air & bone condition (Rinne test)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Asking the client to smile, frown, and wrinkle the forehead tests cranial nerve:
questions.rationale: Facial nerve controls facial expression.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cranial Nerve Assessment (PDF p. 418)
questions.quote: Ask the patient to frown, smile, and wrinkle forehead

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Eliciting the gag reflex and observing uvula rise tests cranial nerve:
questions.rationale: Vagus: gag reflex, symmetric uvula rise, voice.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cranial Nerve Assessment (PDF p. 419)
questions.quote: Observed for symmetric rise of uvula and soft palate

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Loss of the sense of smell is called:
questions.rationale: Anosmia relates to CN I.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cranial Nerve Assessment (PDF p. 418)
questions.quote: anosmia = loss of sense of smell

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Flexing the neck causes involuntary hip and knee flexion. This is:
questions.rationale: Positive Brudzinski's indicates meningeal irritation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Abnormal Reflexes (PDF p. 419)
questions.quote: (+) flexion of hips & knees= (+) meningeal irritation

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: In an adult, stroking the sole causes the toes to fan out. This indicates:
questions.rationale: Toes fanning is abnormal in adults, indicating upper motor neuron lesion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Abnormal Reflexes (PDF p. 419)
questions.quote: Abnormal: toes fan out and draw back

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before a contrast CT scan, the nurse asks about:
questions.rationale: Assess iodine allergy; warn of warm flushing and metallic taste.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CT Scan (PDF p. 420)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before an EEG, the adult client should:
questions.rationale: Sleep deprivation helps; withhold anticonvulsants, sedatives, stimulants as ordered.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EEG (PDF p. 420)
questions.quote: Instruct adult client to sleep no more than 5 hours the night before

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Visual flashes and tingling of the lips before a headache indicate which migraine phase?
questions.rationale: Aura lasts under 1 hour with focal neurologic symptoms.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Migraine Phases (PDF p. 421)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the most common type of headache?
questions.rationale: Tension-type headaches are most common, chronic, and less severe.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Headaches (PDF p. 421)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Sumatriptan is contraindicated in clients with:
questions.rationale: Triptans cause vasoconstriction and chest pain.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-migraine Agents (PDF p. 422)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which environment comforts a client during a migraine?
questions.rationale: Provide a quiet, dark room, HOB at 30 degrees, and analgesics.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Headache Nursing (PDF p. 422)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the earliest sign of increased intracranial pressure?
questions.rationale: LOC change is the earliest sign.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Increased ICP (PDF p. 422)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The upper limit of normal intracranial pressure is about:
questions.rationale: Normal ICP 0–10, upper limit 15 mm Hg.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Increased ICP (PDF p. 422)
